mutants.reason: Request event inverted in IDLE: completer starts a transfer when no request is pending and misses real ones, so no or wrong o_apb_psel.
o_apb_pwakeup resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is high while i_rst_n_slv is low (also breaks the APB4 zero-output rule).
Model's change detection is inverted: delay is applied/updated when the input did not change, so crossing values and latency are wrong.
Pending flag is never set for a delayed change, so a 1 or 2 cycle delayed value never reaches the output and the handshake stalls.

In APB4 (APB5=0) the mutant drives o_wakeup with i_apb_pwakeup, but the completer gates the synchronized wake-up with APB5!=0, so o_apb_pwakeup stays 0 and nothing at the ports changes. It matters only when APB5=1.
The model's pending flag resets to 1, so after reset the cell loads the uninitialised sim_nxt (X) into its output, which propagates to the handshake/outputs.
Delay-counter test inverted, so the extra latencies of 1 and 2 cycles are swapped. Port timing differs for a given seed but stays inside the allowed window, hence it survives.
Requester-side control reset condition inverted: state is held in reset during operation and not reset by i_rst_n_mst.
APB5 gate inverted: in APB4 o_apb_pwakeup is driven active (transfer in progress) and in APB5 it is forced to 0.
In two-phase mode the ack bit is set to 1 instead of toggled, so after the first transfer the ack no longer toggles and later transfers never complete.
Synchronizer chain resets to 1s instead of 0s, so a spurious request/ack/wake-up appears after reset in the synthesis branch.
Reset test inverted in the synthesis 2FF cell: the chain is held at 0 in normal operation and not cleared on reset, so nothing crosses.
The changed branch (HS_TYPE != 0, four-phase ack set to 1) is unreachable in the apb4 run (HS_TYPE=0), so there is no port difference there. In four-phase the ack would never rise.
The changed branch (HS_TYPE != 0, four-phase request set to 1) is unreachable in the apb4 run (HS_TYPE=0), so there is no port difference there. In four-phase no request would be launched.
The line runs only when +APBCDC_MSYNC_EN is given. The apb4 run passes no such plusarg, so sim_en stays 1. It only affects the simulation-model enable switch, which is not specified behaviour.
o_apb_pslverr is set to 1 in the cycle after PREADY instead of cleared, so PSLVERR stays high outside the PREADY cycle (sticky error).
Two-phase ack-event condition inverted (uses the level form), so the requester sees the ack at the wrong time and PREADY is missed or early.
Access phase test of i_apb_pready inverted: the transfer ends while the completer is not ready and waits when it is ready.
In four-phase the ack is not cleared after the request falls (stays 1), so the handshake never closes and the next transfer/PREADY breaks.
Same as M07: the inverted counter test swaps the 1- and 2-cycle extra delays, which changes timing for a seed but stays within the allowed window.
Metastability model is off by default, so crossings use the nominal latency instead of the random 0 to 2 extra cycles. Port timing differs, though it stays in the window.
With zero extra delay the pending flag is set, so the next cycle loads stale or X sim_nxt/sim_cnt into the output.
Zero-extra-delay test inverted: zero extra delay is treated as delayed (stale sim_nxt) and non-zero as immediate, giving wrong and X values.
Request bit launch condition inverted: a request toggles when there is no Setup and not for a real Setup.
The whole term is ANDed with PARA_APBCDC_APB5!=0, which is 0 in the apb4 run, so o_apb_pwakeup is 0 either way. It would change the in-progress wake-up only with APB5=1.
o_apb_psel decode wrong: it is high in IDLE/REQ0 and low in ACCESS for APB4.

In APB4 reg_wakeup is 1 only during reset, then 0 from the first clock because of the APB5 gate. The completer's own APB5 gate keeps o_apb_pwakeup 0, so nothing at the ports changes. It would matter with APB5=1.
w_clr_req is ANDed with HS_TYPE != 0, which is 0 in the apb4 run (two-phase), so it is 0 both ways. It only matters in four-phase, where the request would be cleared in the wrong state.
Response hold register loads when the transfer is not done, so wrong response data/PSLVERR is returned (not the values sampled at completion).
ack resets to 1 while req resets to 0, so after reset the completer sees a spurious request event and starts a transfer with no Setup.
Reset condition of the model chain inverted: the chain is held at the reset value during operation, so no crossing happens.
After the pending value is applied, sim_cur already equals sim_nxt. A stuck sim_pend=1 only reloads the same value each cycle, and the next input change overwrites or clears it, so o_q never differs.
Reset condition inverted for the requester control flops: they are cleared in normal operation and not on reset, so the request never launches and PREADY/ack never appears.
Two-phase request event inverted (req == ack): the completer starts transfers when idle and ignores a real request toggle.
Handshake-type select inverted: two-phase uses the level form of the request, so the event is wrong after the first transfer.
req resets to 1 while ack resets to 0, so after reset a spurious request appears and the completer starts an unrequested transfer.
